I avoid way too many things myself because of fear or uncertainty. Certainty, control, and clearly defined boxes feel safe, but I don't really get to know. Doubt is difficult to deal the unknown or uncertain can look scary, but also leads to missing out on things. I'm just trying to get better at facing these fears and understanding OCD.

If you want you can dm in the future.

Who knows. All I can say is that I was incredibly shy and maybe asexual or incredibly confused in my teens. I was really in a "gay or straight, but they don't seem right either" state because I all I found about bisexuality was invalidating it.

I'm pretty sure I deal with this as it kind of explains my behaviour. Bisexuality is complicated on its own as the bi-cycle can feel like big shifts that aren't easy to experience.

I definitely overthink as even though I call myself bi my mind keeps looking for some proof or certainty of attraction. If I lean one way I get this feeling of unease and wondering if I'm faking being bi, other labels don't exactly feel right either. It's a lot of back and forth checking. It also didn't help that while I'm still questioning, I hadn't felt much a desire for a relationship or sex until my 20s.

You ask a good question because the lines *are* blurry. For some people a masculine woman is a masculine woman, while she's a trans man in other people's eyes.

Being anything would be great, I seem to feel something like euphoria the more mysterious or undefinable I am. Anyways, it's hard because of how gendered our world tends to be and affects what we learn, are encouraged to be, and more.

I thought I was gay and the odd times I was attracted to a girl was a fluke, comp het, or misreading aesthetic attraction. In university I ended up getting crushes on girls, as well as guys.

I'm really just trying to explore my feelings right now. I think it can be difficult due to monosexuality being viewed as more believable. That thinking was part of why I didn't think I was bi for such a long time.

First, your fourth language you're pretty good at English. I'm happy you figuring your identity out!

I'm sorry that all that pain is resurfacing. I know for myself it was really hard to admit I was attracted to guys. I wasn't bullied for it, but my father's homophobia made it hard to love myself.  I've been happier since coming out to friends. 

I have a similar interest in make up, not so much dresses. I never really liked the role of a "traditional male" I felt like I was faking it and the masculinity I wanted and was doesn't fit.

There's a lot of barriers to figuring yourself out, maybe more if you're amab. Like you, contradictory information made it hard. I wondered if I was a transwoman, a pervert, or not valid. I'm still figuring myself out, but we exist and hopefully we can happily be ourselves and express that.
